svg.text: Where cichlids sit among fishes and other vertebrates

text.tspan: human and mouse (ortholog calls), rat, dog, cow, opossum, platypus
not used: several extra genome duplications
zebrafish (ortholog calls), cavefish, catfish; not carps
northern pike; salmon and trout not used
stickleback, fugu, sea bass, seabream, wrasse
convict blenny: the sister family of cichlids
India, Sri Lanka, Madagascar: Etroplus suratensis (Esur)
8 project species, from tilapia to the Lake Malawi haplochromines

svg.text: Blue bold: groups with project species
Black: reference groups already in our trees (examples in grey)
Missing groups: no annotated genome in our trees yet
Grey: groups we deliberately leave out (extra genome duplications complicate orthology)
Whole-genome duplication: 1R and 2R (early vertebrates), 3R (teleosts), and later ones in salmonids, carps and sturgeons; ? = debated
Branch lengths are not to scale. Forks with more than two branches mark relationships that are still debated (among percomorph groups, and among ovalentarian families).
